summary: Trailing-space in tenant header causes session sticky to older model variant during canary promotion
description:
Issue summary:
Customer CloudCart reports intermittent routing to an older quantized model variant for a subset of users after we promoted a canary. The misrouting keeps sessions sticky to the legacy variant (gptx-3.2-quantized-legacy) despite traffic weights set to 0% for the legacy variant.

Impact:
- ~0.8% of requests from CloudCart's tenant for the last 6 hours returned outputs from the legacy quantized model (higher latency, different tokenization), causing content formatting regressions in production-facing features. No increased 5xxs, but quality regressions triggered user complaints.
- Customer on Enterprise/Dedicated tier; risk to SLA and possible rollback request.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (dedicated pool for CloudCart)
- Redwood routing v2.13, edge-proxy v1.8.3, serving-runtime v4.7
- Tenant header used for affinity: X-Tenant

Steps to reproduce (observed in production trace):
1) Send repeated conversations from affected tenant via customer edge (sample header below).
2) Observe sticky session mapping to legacy model over multiple requests, even after new variant is promoted and traffic weight set to 100%.

Observed request header (from ingress logs, redacted):
X-Tenant: cloudcart 
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
User-Agent: CloudCart/2.4

Note: X-Tenant value above contains a trailing space ("cloudcart " ).

Observed behavior:
- Router affinity key normalization occurs upstream in edge-proxy. When the X-Tenant header includes trailing whitespace, the affinity digest generated at the edge differs from the digest used inside the routing service (routing service receives a trimmed header via internal proxy transformation). This mismatch allowed previously sticky sessions to remain bound to the older variant because the session lookup used the non-normalized digest.

Expected behavior:
- Header normalization should be consistent across all components (edge-proxy -> router -> serving), producing identical affinity keys and preventing stale variant sticky retention after a canary promotion.

Logs/traces/evidence:
- Ingress logs (edge-proxy) show requests with X-Tenant values with trailing whitespace for affected cohort (request ids: rq_7b2f, rq_7b3a, rq_7b5e).
- Router lookup logs show session lookup hash H1; edge-proxy shows hash H2 (H1 != H2).
- Serving logs for legacy model show incoming session binds referencing legacy variant id legacy-20260115.
- Link to incident trace: https://sentry.redwood.com/trace/trace-cc-20260219

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally by injecting trailing-space in X-Tenant; edge-proxy code path uses raw header to compute affinity digest, router receives header after an upstream nginx layer which trims whitespace. Root cause appears to be inconsistent normalization responsibilities split between edge-proxy and upstream layer during an earlier refactor (edge-proxy assumed no pre-normalization).
- Hypothesis: customer-side proxy sometimes appends newline/space to headers; we should be defensive.
- Verified that requests with exact same logical tenant but different whitespace map to separate affinity bins and therefore retain older model mapping.

Temporary workaround implemented:
- Applied a short-term edge-proxy config that trims whitespace for X-Tenant before digesting (edge-proxy config hotpatch deployed to prod us-east at 2026-02-19T17:10Z).
- Asked CloudCart to sanitize headers on their end; they confirmed a recent proxy version adds trailing spaces to some headers and will deploy a fix.

Resolution / Next steps:
- Rolled out permanent fix: updated edge-proxy to perform aggressive normalization (trim + collapse internal whitespace) for affinity headers. PRs merged: edge-proxy/pull/2041, router/pull/1219. Deployment schedule: staged rollout to us-east on 2026-02-22, followed by global rollout.
- Added router-side validation to log mismatched header digests to surface future occurrences and to trigger alerts when >0.1% discrepancy is observed.
- Plan to run a 48-hour audit of affinity mismatches across all dedicated pools and alert customers with high mismatch rates.

Follow-up/Action items:
- (SRE) Observe for 72 hours and confirm that legacy model traffic percentage for CloudCart falls to 0.0% (Diego)
- (DX) Update docs for header normalization expectations and recommend defensive client behavior (Maya)
- (Product) Consider exposing an API flag for tenant header normalization for Private deployments (PM meeting scheduled)

Comments / customer communication (excerpt):
- 2026-02-19 18:02 (Support - Maya): "We see a small cohort still hitting the legacy model. We've hotpatched edge to trim tenant headers and asked your proxy team to sanitize headers. We'll monitor and follow up." 
- 2026-02-19 18:28 (CloudCart - support@cloudcart.com): "Thanks — our ops found the proxy bug (trailing-space) and will push a fix. Please let us know when the percentage falls below 0.1%."
- 2026-02-22 09:40 (SRE - Diego): "Staged rollout completed in us-east. Initial audit shows mismatch rate dropped from 0.8% -> 0.02%. Continuing monitoring."

Related artifacts:
- edge-proxy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/2041
- router PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1219
- Internal investigation notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Edge+Header+Normalization

Status update:
- Workaround applied and permanent fix deployed to us-east; monitoring shows expected improvement. Customer notified and satisfied with progress. Action items assigned for audit and docs update.
